transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who might need it more. 

Um... I guess I came in because... well, I've been struggling a little bit lately. I know everyone has their bad days, but I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've... that I've failed. As a father, mostly, and just... as a useful person in general. I feel awful even saying it out loud, I really don't want you to think poorly of me. But the thought just keeps looping in my head, over and over, until I start feeling like I just don't deserve much of a future. 

Is that... does that make sense? Am I answering your question right?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, even activities you used to like?

Well, I... I suppose I have noticed a bit of a change there. I mean, I really don't want to sound ungrateful for the things I have, but... yes. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, or, you know, watching the Cubs games with my daughter. We always had such a nice time doing that together. 

But lately... I just can't seem to find the joy in it. The trains are just sitting there half-built on the table, gathering dust. And even just turning on the TV to put a game on... it just feels sort of pointless right now. I feel terrible admitting that, especially about the things with my daughter. I know I should be trying harder to be present for her. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... I'd say it's been... well, maybe about a month? I feel a little silly even admitting that, to be honest, because... well, it started right around the time my daughter left for college out of state. 

I know I should just be thrilled for her, and I am, I really am. She worked so hard to get in. But ever since she packed up and moved... I've just been sort of stuck in this rut. I really hope you don't think I'm just being some overly attached, pathetic dad. I know kids have to grow up and leave the nest, and I really don't want to make her milestone about me. But yeah, it's been about four weeks of just... not being able to snap out of it. 

Does that... is that helpful for your notes? Am I explaining the timeline okay?
Have you been having trouble sleeping through the night or waking up much earlier than usual, even when you’re tired?

Um... well, yes, actually. I feel a little bad complaining about it because I know I have all day to rest if I need to, but sleep has been... it's been a bit of a struggle lately. 

I try to keep a normal schedule, I really do. But I just end up lying in bed for hours. The house is just so quiet now, you know? And then... well, when I finally do manage to drift off, I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. 

Once my eyes are open, I just can't get back to sleep. My mind just starts running through... well, through everything I feel like I've messed up. I try so hard to just shut it off and think about positive things, but my brain just won't let it go. I hope I don't sound completely neurotic admitting that. I know I should be better at controlling my thoughts at my age. 

Is that... does that answer what you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details for your evaluation.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety without being able to relax?

Um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I might be a little sluggish some mornings, but who isn't, right? Especially when you're not sleeping well. I try to make sure I'm still getting up and moving around the house so I don't just turn into a complete lump. 

And as for being fidgety... no, I don't think I'm pacing the halls or anything like that. I really try to just stay calm and not let myself get too worked up. I hope that's a good thing? I know you're looking for specific symptoms, so I hope it's okay that I don't really have that one to report. Does that sound normal to you?
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level or felt unusually tired lately, even when you're not doing much?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I have been feeling pretty tired. I feel awful even saying it, because, like you said, I'm really not doing much these days since I'm not working. I don't want to sound lazy, I promise I'm not trying to be. 

But it's just... even the simple things, like carrying a basket of laundry up the stairs or just standing there sorting through the mail... it feels like I'm trying to move through wet cement. And it doesn't seem to matter how long I've been lying in bed, the exhaustion is just... it's just always there, weighing me down. 

I try to push through it, I really do, because I know I should be more productive with my time. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses for not getting things done around the house. Is that the kind of fatigue you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um... well, I suppose my appetite has been a little off lately. I hate to even admit it, because I know I should be taking better care of myself and eating right. But... most days, I just don't really bother making a real meal. I hope that doesn't sound too irresponsible of me. 

It's just that I sort of forget to eat until it gets quite late in the day, and by then, I usually only manage to have a piece of toast or a bowl of cereal. I actually noticed the other day that I've had to tighten my belt a notch or two, so I guess I have lost some weight without really meaning to. 

I'm really going to try to do better and start making proper dinners again, I promise. I know you doctors always emphasize a balanced diet. Does that... does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information for your notes.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down and lost interest in things, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um... well, no, I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. I mean, everyone has their off days, right? Or times when they're just feeling a little blue or unmotivated. I've definitely had moments where I've felt stressed or sad about things, but I always managed to just... bounce back, you know? 

I've always tried to be a positive person and keep moving forward. I really pride myself on being resilient. So, this... this heaviness that just won't lift, and not wanting to do the things I usually enjoy... this is really the first time it's been this bad, or lasted this long. 

I hope it doesn't make me seem weak, that I'm struggling so much right now. I'm really trying my best to snap out of it. Is it... is it normal for something like this to just happen for the first time at my age? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or anything.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Um... well... I know this is a really important question, and I want to be completely honest with you, but I... I feel terrible even bringing this up. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or that I'm giving up, because I'm really trying not to. 

But... sometimes, lately, I've just been having these thoughts that... well, that maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Just to stop feeling so heavy all the time. I'd never want to cause a fuss or leave a mess for anyone else, I promise. 

Actually, that's sort of what scared me the other day. I... I caught myself going through all my financial paperwork, organizing my accounts and things... almost like I was getting it all ready for someone else to take over. When I realized what I was doing, it really frightened me. I don't want to be that kind of person, I really don't. 

I hope you don't judge me too harshly for having those thoughts. I know I should be stronger than this. Is it... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you the truth.
